Subject: Re: Sudden throughput & 5xx spike on inference endpoints — initial triage

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the net team side (09:30–09:40 window):

- Peering state: VPC peering session between us and OrbitLane's VPC showed transient route withdrawal on one path starting 08:49 PDT. We observed BGP flap events on the transit peer and asymmetric routing for a subset of /24s.
- DNS: Our edge resolvers intermittently returned IP A records from a stale NVA (internal nat viv) due to EDNS client subnet propagation mismatch; TTLs overlapped with a stale cached answer at ~09:05.
- Proxy/firewall: When the backend TCP handshakes experienced a 200–500ms increase we saw proxy timeouts translating to 504s rather than queued retries.

Attachments: route-table-dump.txt (snippet below) and a short log excerpt.

[attachment: route-table-dump.txt (text)]

Immediate mitigation steps already in flight:
- 09:28: enabled failover route to warm replica pool in us-west-2 (no config change required from OrbitLane) — this reduced error rates from 35% to ~12% for traffic hitting the warm pool.
- 09:36: increased proxy connect-timeout to allow 1s extra handshake (temporary) to reduce 504 conversion.

Next: I recommend a coordinated DNS cache flush on OrbitLane resolvers (if they control them) and a short-lived BGP dampening reset on the transit peer. If OrbitLane can accept a temporary route override we can move ~70% of traffic off the impacted peered path immediately.

Will keep updates coming.

— Rishi
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Arjun / Eva,

Thanks for the fast report and for the pcap. Quick status: we've identified the peering path instability and a DNS cache race that together are creating asymmetric flows and occasional blackholing. Rishi's team has already moved a subset of traffic to the warm replica pool which reduced error rate materially but not fully to SLA targets.

To accelerate restoration we need your approval to perform a short-lived, traffic-level routing override (up to 60 minutes) that will steer your production namespace to an alternate egress in us-west-2 while we remediate the peering and DNS caches. This does not require you to change your infra but will change traffic egress at the edge for a subset of prefixes.

If you approve we will:
- Implement the override at 10:15 PDT
- Monitor error rate and latency every 5 minutes and rollback automatically if error rate increases
- Share an incident timeline and collect tcpdumps from both sides for the postmortem

Please reply with a quick OK and whether you want us to apply the override.

Eva / Arjun / team,

Thank you for the quick coordination and permission to proceed. Final summary (chronological):

- 08:49 PDT — Transit peer BGP instability caused transient route withdrawals for a subset of OrbitLane prefixes.
- 09:05 PDT — DNS resolver cache returned a stale internal nat IP for some clients due to EDNS propagation mismatch.
- 09:28 PDT — Redwood applied failover to warm replica pool; error rate decreased from ~35% to ~12%.
- 10:15 PDT — With your approval we implemented a 60-minute routing override to us-west-2 egress. Error rate fell below 1.5% and tail latency returned to baseline within 12 minutes.

What we changed and why:
- Routing override: moved traffic off the affected peered path to avoid packet loss and asymmetric NAT translation.
- Temporary proxy timeout bump: reduced 504 conversions while backends completed handshakes.
- Coordinated cache invalidation: both sides flushed DNS caches to remove stale A records.

Attachments we've collected: orbitlane_pcap_20290707.zip, route-table-dump.txt, slo-dashboard-screenshot.png. We will keep these for the postmortem.

Action items and owners:
- Redwood (Rishi): coordinate with transit peer to dampen BGP flaps and provide route-flap logs (ETA 24 hours).
- OrbitLane (Arjun/Eva): confirm DNS cache flush completed and provide any resolver configs changed in the last 72 hours.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare incident timeline and draft postmortem (first draft within 48 hours).
- Redwood (Jonas): follow up on credit & SLA exception request with Finance/Legal and loop you back (ETA 48–72 hours).

We understand this reached your execs and apologize for the disruption. We'll deliver a full RCA and remediation plan, and share proposed hardening (BGP dampening policy, DNS TTL recommendations, and an automated routing fallback).

If you'd like, let's schedule a 30-minute postmortem on Thursday 2029-07-11 to review findings. I will create the calendar invite.
